consensus_summary: Blind responses converge on oil primarily symbolizing the Holy Spirit (anointing, empowering, consecrating presence), with common secondary senses of healing, joy/gladness, consecration/setting apart, and (less centrally) abundance or lamp-fuel readiness/light; Spirit is treated as the settled or dominant Christian association.
book_summary: Oil is the pressed, tested fruit of the olive—proven works that make light; explicitly not the Spirit.
rationale: The book directly negates and displaces the primary consensus identification (Holy Spirit via anointing) that all three blind responses report as dominant, substituting instead a works/light reading drawn from lamp and virgin-parable contexts; this is contradiction rather than refinement or novelty outside the field.
strongest_objection: The printed citations support oil-as-lamp-fuel and a works-light link via Matt 5:16 but supply no textual basis for the explicit rejection of the Spirit or for equating oil itself with proven works, while major anointing passages that drive the consensus Spirit reading are omitted.
